::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Hamiltonian Approach](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2459249/hamiltonian-approach), asked by [user1611542](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/360341/user1611542) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-10-05; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Solve the plane pendulum problem using the Hamiltonian approach and show that H is a constant of motion.
>
> **Approach :**  Assuming it means simple pendulum by plane pendulum, I have calculated Hamiltonian as a function of $\theta , l$ (Length of pendulum) ,$\ p_\theta$
>
> But what does it mean by H is a constant of motion ?
:::

"of motion" is a physics idiom, and I'm not sure what it adds to the statement.  You want to show
$$\frac{dH}{dt} = \frac{\partial H}{\partial \theta}\dot \theta
                   +\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_{\theta}}\dot p_\theta = 0$$
